title: Managed investment schemes: Interests not for money
subject: This guide addresses ASIC's approach to providing relief from managed investment, AFS licensing, anti-hawking, and product disclosure provisions of the Corporations Act 2001 for certain managed investment schemes that arise from business or professional arrangements and do not involve raising money.
background: The guide is issued under the Corporations Act 2001 and explains conditional relief for interests-not-for-money schemes, including show schemes and film investment schemes. It is intended for operators and promoters of such schemes who seek relief from regulatory obligations.
ruling: ASIC provides conditional relief from the managed investment, AFS licensing, anti-hawking, and product disclosure provisions for interests-not-for-money schemes that meet specific criteria, such as those arising from business or professional arrangements. The relief is set out in ASIC Corporations (Managed Investment Schemes: Interests Not For Money) Instrument 2016/1107. ASIC interprets the law to exclude these schemes from certain regulatory requirements where no money is raised and the interests are not offered to the public. The guide explains the conditions for relief, including for show schemes and film investment schemes, and outlines ASIC's regulatory approach to ensuring investor protection while facilitating legitimate business arrangements.
